classification.difficultyReason: Compare negative coefficients, select the third-quadrant auxiliary angle and solve the resulting cosine equation on the stated domain.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express $-\cos x-\sin x$ in the form $D\cos(x-\varphi)$, where $D>0$ and $0<\varphi<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}-\cos x-\sin x&=D\cos x\cos\varphi+D\sin x\sin\varphi\\D\cos\varphi&=-1\\D\sin\varphi&=-1\\D^2(\cos^2\varphi+\sin^2\varphi)&=(-1)^2+(-1)^2\\D&=\sqrt{2}\quad(D>0)\\\tan\varphi&=1\end{aligned}$$
Since $\cos\varphi<0$ and $\sin\varphi<0$, $\varphi$ is in quadrant III.
$$\begin{aligned}\varphi&=\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{5\pi}{4}\\-\cos x-\sin x&=\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence solve $-\cos x-\sin x=1$, for $0\le x<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)&=1\\\cos\left(x-\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$$
The transformed domain is $-\frac{5\pi}{4}\le x-\frac{5\pi}{4}<\frac{3\pi}{4}$.
$$\begin{aligned}x-\frac{5\pi}{4}&=-\frac{\pi}{4}\text{ or }\frac{\pi}{4}\\x&=\pi\text{ or }\frac{3\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$$
